describes: The engineering substrate: what runs, what it was measured at, and why each choice was made rather than defaulted.
note: Every figure here is either read from a committed file or recorded in the build log. Nothing is projected, rounded up, or copied from a vendor benchmark. Where a number has not been measured yet the entry says so instead of estimating one.

hardware.why: The constraint is the point. Every decision below — fp16, batch size, model choice, co-residency — was forced by an 8 GB budget rather than chosen on a machine where it did not matter.

decisions.evidence: Measured on a tuning sweep: defaults reached 0.836 overall recall, the tuned parameters reached 0.998.
decisions.cost: Index build cost roughly triples. Paid once per ingest, never on the query path.
decisions.why: A vector index shipped on defaults is an untested assumption. The sweep turned it into a number with a price attached.

decisions.decision: Reciprocal rank fusion over ranks, k=60
decisions.alternative: Normalising and summing BM25 and cosine scores
decisions.evidence: BM25 scores and cosine similarities are not on comparable scales; any normalisation encodes an assumption that is wrong differently for every query.
decisions.cost: Discards score magnitude, keeping only order.
decisions.why: Fusing by position needs no assumption about either scale. It is the cheaper claim to defend.

decisions.decision: 5 passages of 700 characters, max 2,048 output tokens, temperature 0
decisions.evidence: A 3B model given ten 1,200-character passages produced no claims at all. Fewer, shorter passages left it enough attention to copy a quote accurately.
decisions.cost: Less context per answer, so recall of the retriever matters more.
decisions.why: Verbatim quoting is what the citation check verifies. A context budget that defeats quoting defeats the verification.

decisions.decision: Schema-constrained decoding via XGrammar under vLLM
decisions.alternative: Asking for JSON in the prompt and parsing what comes back
decisions.evidence: The answer schema becomes a decoding constraint rather than a request, so citations are parseable by construction.
decisions.cost: Ties generation to a serving stack that supports grammars.
decisions.why: A citation format that depends on the model's goodwill is not a format.

decisions.alternative: fp32, or a larger embedding model
decisions.evidence: 51,310 chunks embedded in 1.5 minutes at 558 chunks/s, producing 79 MB of vectors. 6.87 GB of the 8 GB budget remained free with the embedder loaded.
decisions.cost: A smaller embedding model than the leaderboards favour.
decisions.why: Headroom was the requirement: the embedder and the generator have to be co-resident on one 8 GB card.

decisions.decision: PostgreSQL row-level security inside the retrieval query, under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role
decisions.alternative: Filtering results in application code after retrieval
decisions.evidence: The application connection asserts rolsuper=false and rolbypassrls=false before it is handed to a caller. A superuser is exempt from RLS silently — no error, no warning.
decisions.cost: Post-filtering an approximate index costs recall, which is measured and reported separately rather than folded into headline numbers.
decisions.why: Access control enforced in application code is a control that a bug can skip. Enforced in the query, it is a control the database applies.

decisions.decision: One partition and one index per tenant
decisions.alternative: A single index across all tenants on the parent table
decisions.evidence: A partitioned index on the parent is built across every tenant, which loses the property that makes partitioning useful.
decisions.cost: More indexes to build and maintain.
decisions.why: A tenant's data being in its own partition is what makes isolation structural rather than a WHERE clause.

evaluation.detail: Each published run differs from the baseline by exactly one configuration key, so any difference is attributable to that key. The comparison view flags it when more than one differs.
1,000 resamples of the query set on every quality metric. A delta whose intervals overlap is reported as not separated rather than given a number that looks decisive.

evaluation.practice: The judge is measured, not trusted
evaluation.detail: Relevance grades are drafted by a pinned model and a stratified sample is re-graded by hand. Of 32 judgments checked so far the human and the model agreed on 4. No retrieval score is published until that is understood.

evaluation.practice: Failure modes are published, not hidden
evaluation.detail: Nine documented failure modes, each marked observed or prevented-by-design, each naming the metrics it corrupts and how it was detected.
Script, regenerate command, commit and corpus id sit beside each figure, so a number can be traced to the code that produced it.
No placeholder figures and no illustrative values anywhere. A run that has not happened renders as an empty state naming the phase that delivers it.

guardrails.detail: Six narrow pattern classes — override, role reassignment, chat-role markers, tag injection, exfiltration, answer override. Removals are counted and marked in the chunk, never silent, and the patterns are deliberately narrow so ordinary contract and standards prose survives.

guardrails.control: Retrieved text cannot forge prompt structure
guardrails.detail: Each passage is fenced and the fence literal is stripped from the body first, so a document cannot impersonate the header of a passage that was never retrieved.

guardrails.control: Citations must resolve to passages actually shown
guardrails.detail: A cited chunk id is checked against the set the model was given. A citation to anything else fails rather than being displayed.

guardrails.control: Quotes are checked character by character
guardrails.detail: Each quoted span is matched against the source text, with the longest verbatim run recorded so an altered quote is distinguishable from an invented one.
The system declines when the evidence does not support an answer, and how often it declines correctly is one of the reported metric families rather than a footnote.

stack.choice: Postgres GIN over tsvector, BM25-style scoring
Row-level security, non-superuser role, per-tenant partitions
Gemini, pinned to dated snapshots, human-verified sample
Next.js static export, no runtime, no backend
